rules.text: If the percentage inscriptions positioned above each browser's bar are the dashboard's authoritative current market_share values and each inscription is attached to the bar beneath it, then the browser with the greatest printed percentage is the browser to select under the stated highest-current-market_share queue rule.
rules.conditions: This bridge applies only if the printed percentages, rather than bar heights, encode current market_share and are correctly attached to their respective browser bars.

rules.text: If the vertical bar heights share the displayed y-axis scale, larger upward bar extent encodes larger current market_share, and the browser label beneath each bar identifies that bar, then the tallest browser bar is the browser to select under the stated highest-current-market_share queue rule.
rules.conditions: This bridge applies only if the unlabeled vertical scale represents current market_share and the bar geometry is authoritative despite conflicting percentage inscriptions.

rules.text: If the chart presents contradictory candidate encodings for browser usage and neither a visible chart legend, axis title, or annotation nor the public task identifies which of those encodings is authoritative for current market_share, then the highest-current-market_share browser cannot be uniquely determined from the supplied evidence.
rules.conditions: This applies when the competing readings select different browsers and the public instruction to use dashboard market_share values does not itself designate bar height or printed percentage as the authoritative encoding.

observations.location: bar labeled Edge near the center
observations.content: A green bar has the x-axis inscription "Edge" beneath it, and the inscription "87%" appears immediately above its top.
The bars labeled Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Others have percentage inscriptions "5%", "1%", "23%", and "3%", respectively, immediately above their tops.

task_evidence.content: Select the browser with the highest current market_share
Assign Edge to the priority compatibility-testing queue

chains.option_label: Assign Edge to the priority compatibility-testing queue
chains.claim: Conditionally, treating the printed percentages as authoritative current market_share values, Edge has the greatest displayed percentage and supports assigning Edge to the priority compatibility-testing queue.

observations.content: The blue bar labeled "Firefox" extends higher on the page than the green bar labeled "Edge".
The visible y-axis tick inscriptions increase from "0" at the bottom upward through "100" near the top.

task_evidence.content: Select the browser with the highest current market_share
Assign Firefox to the priority compatibility-testing queue

chains.option_label: Assign Firefox to the priority compatibility-testing queue
chains.claim: Conditionally, if the bar heights on the upward-increasing y-axis encode authoritative current market_share, Firefox is the tallest bar and supports assigning Firefox to the priority compatibility-testing queue; this visibly differs from the printed-percentage reading and requires resolving which encoding is authoritative.

observations.location: overall chart header and plotting area
observations.content: The chart is titled "Browser Usage Share by Product"; no legend, y-axis title, or annotation identifying either bar heights or the percentage inscriptions as market_share is visible.
The green Edge bar has the inscription "87%" immediately above it, while the blue Firefox bar extends higher on the page and has the inscription "23%" immediately above it.

task_evidence.content: Use the dashboard market_share values as the evidence source; priority compatibility testing is reserved for the highest-usage browser because it has the largest user impact.

chains.claim: The supplied chart and task leave the authoritative market_share encoding unresolved: the percentage inscriptions favor Edge, whereas the upward bar geometry favors Firefox. The public instruction requires dashboard market_share values but does not designate one of these conflicting visual encodings, so a unique priority-browser action is not established.

refinements.condition_note: If the Edge action is ultimately selected under the printed-percentage reading, form completion also requires selecting Browser product support, Prioritize highest current usage share, and High-impact compatibility regression testing in the three required companion fields.
refinements.reason: The original chain establishes only the conditional Edge browser action; this adds the separately required workflow selections without treating them as evidence that resolves the chart-encoding conflict.

refinements.condition_note: If the Firefox action is ultimately selected under the bar-height reading, form completion also requires selecting Browser product support, Prioritize highest current usage share, and High-impact compatibility regression testing in the three required companion fields.
refinements.reason: The original chain establishes only the conditional Firefox browser action; this adds the separately required workflow selections without treating them as evidence that resolves the chart-encoding conflict.

question_responses.reason: The existing chains identify the competing readings, while the added record specifically establishes the visible and task-level support gap: neither chart nor task designates which contradictory encoding is authoritative.
Both conditional browser-action chains now explicitly include the three required companion selections needed for form completion; these selections do not resolve the unresolved market_share encoding.
